whatItDoes: Converts an amount from one currency to another using live exchange rates for 160+ world currencies. Rates are fetched from a public exchange-rate API and cached for 10 minutes. Shows the converted amount, the exchange rate applied, and a clearly visible rate timestamp so you always know how current the number is.
whyItExists: Exchange rates move constantly and using a stale or wrong rate can misprice an invoice, budget, or travel plan. This tool gives a current, clearly dated rate in one click, plus context on how the mid-market rate differs from what banks charge.
whoShouldUse: Freelancers and contractors invoicing across currencies, travelers budgeting abroad, online shoppers price-comparing, importers quoting in foreign currency, and anyone handling foreign currency transactions.
useCases: Convert an invoice amount into your home currency before sending a quote
Check what a foreign price actually equals in your currency before paying
Estimate travel spending and build a daily budget for a trip
Compare international prices when shopping online across marketplaces
Verify a rate quoted by a bank or payment gateway against the live mid-market rate
Convert project budgets between the currencies your clients pay in
instructions: Enter the amount you want to convert
Choose the source currency (From) — the currency the amount is in
Choose the target currency (To) — the currency you want the result in
Read the converted amount and the exchange rate used, along with its timestamp
Press Refresh rates to load a fresh rate after 10 minutes
Swap the From and To currencies with the swap button to check the reverse rate
bestPractices: Use a recent rate for accurate quotes, since rates change constantly
Keep in mind banks and card networks add a margin over the mid-market rate — often 1-3%
Refresh the rates once more right before a real transaction
Confirm the target currency code for the country you need (e.g., EUR vs. GBP)
For large transfers, compare the tool's rate with what your bank actually quotes
commonMistakes: Using a stale rate from memory or an old page
Confusing the From and To direction, which inverts the conversion
Assuming the rate shown is the final rate after bank fees and margins
Mixing currency codes (USD vs US dollar abbreviations) or using the wrong country's currency
Forgetting that weekend rates are often frozen and Monday markets can gap
faq: Where do the rates come from? — A public exchange-rate API refreshed every 10 minutes.
Why are rates cached for 10 minutes? — To keep the tool fast and avoid hammering the free API; a 10-minute window is fine for planning.
Are these the rates my bank gives? — No. Banks and cards add fees or margins on top of the mid-market rate.
Is my data shared? — No. Only the shared rate table is fetched; no personal data leaves your browser.
Does the conversion include transfer fees? — No. It shows the raw currency conversion; add any transfer or service fees separately.
Why does the rate keep changing? — The foreign-exchange market trades 24/5 and rates reflect the latest market prices.
